name: Tahash
title: Son of Nahor
summary: Tahash was one of the eight sons of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his concubine Reumah. He is mentioned in the genealogy in Genesis 22 as part of Abraham's extended family. Tahash is a lesser-known biblical figure, but his lineage is important for understanding the family relationships surrounding the patriarchs.
relatedPersons: Maacah, son of Nahor and his concubine Reumah

keyEvents.title: The sons of Nahor and Reumah
keyEvents.description: Tahash is mentioned as one of the sons of Nahor and his concubine Reumah, in connection with the news Abraham received about his brother's family.

keyEvents.title: Abraham's Family News
keyEvents.description: After the binding of Isaac, Abraham learned about his brother Nahor's children, including Tahash. This news connected Abraham to his extended family in Mesopotamia.

keyEvents.title: Reumah's Role as Concubine
keyEvents.description: Tahash was born to Reumah, who was Nahor's concubine, a common practice during the time of the patriarchs. This placed Tahash in a secondary lineage compared to Nahor's sons with his primary wife Milcah.

keyEvents.title: The Kinship of Bethuel and Rebekah
keyEvents.description: Through his father Nahor, Tahash was related to Bethuel, who was the son of Nahor and Milcah, and thus also related to Rebekah, who later became Isaac's wife.
